newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold market to shine with Indian reforms.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold market to shine with Indian reforms.

text.p: Dubai's gold market should get a shot in the arm as a result of Indian monetary reform and the upcoming festival season, Dubai gold traders said on Sunday.

"The new monetary policy announced by Reserve Bank of India will improve the liquidity and upcoming festival and wedding season augurs well for the Indian bullion market," Sultan Satani, managing director of Satco Global Trading said.

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) -- India's central bank -- on Saturday announced steps to boost domestic liquidity, increase the flow of bank funds into stock and commodity markets and raise export credits.
Analysts have generally warmed to the measures saying that it may reverse economic slow down and promote growth.

Dubai bullion traders also welcomed the news on Sunday saying that the reforms, combined with a good Indian monsoon, the upcoming festival and wedding season and stable bullion prices gave the Dubai market a bullish outlook.
"We had good rains. The crops will be good and buying for the wedding season is strong," one souk seller said.
Dubai is India's main feeder market into India -- the world's single largest gold market -- with some 80 percent of the gold imported into the Gulf emirate re-exported to the Indian subcontinent.

Indian demand for gold from Dubai traditionally takes off from late October to meet demand for two major Hindu festivals -- Dassera (victory of good over evil) and Diwali (festival of lights) -- and the country's second main marriage season.
World Gold Council Middle East and India chief executive Rolf Schneebeli estimates India gold demand is estimated to hit 500 tonnes in 1996, up from 477 tonnes in 1995.

Demand from the Indian subcontinent is also expected to be encouraged this year by relatively low bullion prices while Dubai turn-over is also expected to get a boost from the tourist trade that is now beginning.
World spot bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $380.00-$380.50 an ounce, compared to $382-383 year-on-year.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,254 UAE dirhams ($1,431.60), down from 5,265 dirhams on October 13.
Ten gram gold pieces shed one dirham to 449 dirhams.
TT bars in the Bombay market were assessed at $1,691 dirhams, an attractive Dubai-Bombay trading arbitrage. ($1=3.67 UAE dirhams)
